data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew name Malachi, meaning 'my god is King'. In the Bible, Melchiades is mentioned as a high priest in Jerusalem during the time of the Maccabean Revolt. His devotion to God and leadership inspired the Jewish people to reclaim the temple from the Greeks. The name Melchiades carries the meaning “King of righteousness” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Melchiades usually hope their child will grow to embody king of righteousness and live with faith, good character and purpose.
